answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with collateralized peer vouching: a new identity only earns full rights when established agents stake funds vouching for it, like a jetty that only opens after trusted harbours confirm the ship. If the vouched agent cheats, every voucher loses part of its stake, so creating fake identities means risking real capital per identity. Vouches also expire, like an orchard that must be re-tended each season, and an isolated island of mutually vouching fakes earns no outside trust, so scale brings cost, not free identities.
